subject: Invoice timing / daylight-savings pro-rate + VAT handling for Nov window
messages:
From: Oliver King <oliver.king@greenfield.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Greenfield Billing <billing@greenfield.ai>
Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: High Nov 1 usage on invoice / timezone attribution question

Hi Marissa,

We pulled our November invoice (INV-2026-11-01) and are seeing a ~24% spike on the 1st that doesn't correlate with any backend changes on our side. The spike appears entirely in tokens for the midnight UTC ingest window (our batch job runs 00:00 UTC).

A few specifics:
- Invoice line: "Text generation - usage" dated 2026-11-01 shows 2,482,310 tokens.
- Our internal logs show 1,990,470 tokens attributed to 2026-11-01 UTC.
- The delta appears to be tokens recorded in Redwood with a 2026-10-31 PST timestamp (prior billing day) then reconciled into Nov 1 on your invoice.

Can you confirm how Redwood rounds/assigns usage across day boundaries and whether a DST/timezone shift could have caused retroactive attribution? We suspect a clock/bucket alignment issue around the daylight-savings change in early November.

We need:
1) Raw usage rows for 2026-10-31 through 2026-11-02 (UTC and PST timestamps) so we can reconcile.
2) Recommendation: either adjust the Nov invoice (pro-rata correction) or issue a credit.
3) VAT handling: Greenfield is an EU legal entity and needs to know if the credit will be issued gross or net of VAT, or if you can issue a corrected invoice with reverse-charge applied. I can attach our VAT cert if needed.

I've attached a sample of our ingestion job CSV and the invoice line for quick reference (see attachment stub: usage_export_20261110.csv).

Thanks — would appreciate a response by EOD tomorrow if possible.

— Oliver
Oliver King
Finance Ops | Greenfield Analytics

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Oliver King <oliver.king@greenfield.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 11:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: High Nov 1 usage on invoice / timezone attribution question

Hi Oliver — thanks for the clear breakdown and the CSV. I’m looping in Ben from billing and Priya on tax so we can get you an audit and proposed remediation.

Ben / Priya: Oliver flagged an apparent cross-day attribution spike around the DST transition. Please pull: (a) per-request rows for 2026-10-31 to 2026-11-02 including both UTC and server-local timestamps, request_ids, model, and token counts; (b) the service-side aggregation windows used to bucket usage for invoicing. Oliver noted a preference for an invoice correction vs a credit but can confirm after we propose options.

Oliver: we’ll aim to get a preliminary reconciliation and options by tomorrow EOD PST. If you can confirm VAT registration (VAT ID + cert), Priya can advise on reverse-charge vs credit memo netting.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.ai>, Oliver King <oliver.king@greenfield.ai>
Date: Wed, 11 Nov 2026 09:27:00 -0800
Subject: RE: High Nov 1 usage on invoice / timezone attribution question

Hi team — quick update from billing ops after an initial look:

Findings (preliminary):
- Root cause likely a combination of our aggregation cut-over window (midnight PST bucket) and an ingestion clock edge on the customer side. When requests arrive within a narrow 90s window around midnight local, our sampler historically used server-local epoch that was adjusted for DST incorrectly in one aggregation job run on 2026-11-01.
- Result: ~490k tokens were double-attributed at the bucket boundary on a subset of requests (these look like replays where both pre- and post-aggregation events were recorded).

Options we recommend:
1) Issue a corrected invoice for Nov (remove the double-attributed tokens) and publish a corrected PDF + credit memo. This is our preferred path if the customer prefers bookkeeping tidy records.
2) Leave the original invoice in place and issue a pro-rated credit on the next invoice (faster to execute but requires acceptance that the original invoice and VAT line will have been applied).

Tax note (Priya): credits are usually issued net of VAT (i.e., we adjust tax lines on the credit memo). If the customer wants a corrected invoice with reverse-charge applied, we need: (a) legal entity VAT ID, (b) confirmation that the supply is cross-border B2B, and (c) any supporting docs to mark the invoice zero-rated.

Estimate & timeline:
- Audit export: I’ve placed a scoped export in the shared audit folder (link in related links).
- If customer wants a corrected invoice, finance can issue corrected invoice + credit memo in 2–3 business days after we have final sign-off and VAT docs.

Action items: Oliver — please confirm preferred option and share VAT ID/certificate if you want reverse-charge treatment. Marissa — I’ll draft the credit memo language once Oliver confirms.

Attachments referenced: usage_export_20261110.csv (customer-provided), billing_audit_slice_202611.zip (internal stub).

— Ben Carter
Billing Ops | Redwood Inference

From: Oliver King <oliver.king@greenfield.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 12 Nov 2026 14:15:00 -0800
Subject: Re: High Nov 1 usage on invoice / timezone attribution question

Thanks Ben — that flow makes sense. We’d prefer a corrected invoice (option 1) so our accounting records match the month. I’ve attached our VAT certificate and VAT ID below.

VAT ID: EU-GF-7781923
Attachment stub: vat_registration_GF.pdf

Please proceed with the corrected invoice route. For audit purposes, can you also include a one-line explanation on the credit memo referencing the aggregation window shift and token double-attribution? That will help our AP team accept the correction without a separate audit.

If you need anything else from our side, let me know. Otherwise please confirm expected date for the corrected docs.

— Oliver

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Oliver King <oliver.king@greenfield.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 14 Nov 2026 16:40:00 -0800
Subject: Final: corrected invoice + credit memo timeline

Oliver — thank you for confirming and for the VAT cert. We’ll proceed with option 1 (corrected invoice). Summary and next steps: 

- What we’ll deliver: corrected invoice PDF (INV-2026-11-01-R1) + credit memo that removes the ~490k double-attributed tokens and adjusts VAT accordingly. The credit memo will include the line: "Adjustment for aggregation-window double-attribution (see audit slice GF-2026-11-01)."
- VAT handling: accounting will issue the corrected invoice with reverse-charge / zero-rated VAT line since we have the VAT ID on file (EU-GF-7781923). The credit memo will reflect the tax adjustment so your AP sees a net change consistent with reverse-charge treatment.
- Timeline: corrected PDF + credit memo by Wed, 18 Nov 2026 EOD PST (3 business days).
- Next steps for customer: please confirm the bill-to legal name as it should appear on the corrected invoice (we will use the name on your VAT cert unless you specify otherwise).

I’ve attached the corrected invoice stub for tracking (corrected_invoice_GF-202611.pdf) — final will be delivered with a DocuSign-ready packet if required. HubSpot ticket updated: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/ticket/GF-1147.

If anything changes or you need the credit memo earlier, we can expedite but would need a quick sign-off on the credit language.

Best regards,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
